note: The blank donor (variable 15662) is pinned to the slug answer-sweden, which its documented-blank `[[representation.matrix]]` also gives the answer variable it converts, so the window's FQID names two compiled variable keys: the donor's and the answer's, which extends the donor's key as the replaced test's `(*key, "split")` did. The refusal is overbroad, ahead of the edition checks: the pooled edition '2012 - 2014' alone would make the entry stale. The donor publishes no variable. Since maintainer decision 11 the shared slug is itself refused (`naming_slug_collision` on the donor and the answer, which is then withheld): that refusal is pinned by `naming-slug-collision-refuses-a-blank-matrix-donor-named-like-its-answer`, whose source this case shares, so this case projects only the window's issue. The alias windows compile before the merged-scope slug check, so the window still sees both keys.
fails_if: `compile_alias_windows` (curation_compile.py) stops refusing a variable FQID that resolves to more than one compiled key, or checks the editions first, so the entry is reported stale (or binds one of the two variables) instead of overbroad

sources.description: SCB register 257 (variant 553) delivers one blank-column source instance (var_id 15662, CVID 400684, edition '2012 - 2014') whose value set is the single code 1/Yes; no Unika file.
